priorStories.headline: Moscow park closes after U.S. security warning
priorStories.body:
Russia temporarily closed Moscow’s Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve and restricted access to its park after receiving a U.S. warning about preparations for a possible terrorist attack.

Russia’s Federal Security Service said the warning came through established channels. The U.S. Embassy separately described a credible threat of a mass-casualty event at the complex.

candidates.summary: Portuguese police dismantled housing-protest camps in Lisbon’s Rossio Square and Porto’s Dom João I Square at about 4:30 a.m. local time. Police dispersed protesters in Lisbon using shields and baton charges. AFP reported that police said six people were arrested in Lisbon and seven in Porto for refusing orders to disperse. The camps followed Saturday marches opposing a rental bill that protesters say would worsen housing affordability.
candidates.title: Police clear housing-protest camps in Lisbon and Porto

candidates.summary: Thousands of students and supporters marched silently in Novi Sad and held a moment of silence on the second anniversary of the railway-station canopy collapse that killed 16 people. Participants placed 16 wreaths and 16 red hearts outside the station. The disaster had triggered a two-year anti-corruption movement that defeated Aleksandar Vučić’s governing party in parliamentary elections a week earlier.
candidates.title: Thousands commemorate Novi Sad station-collapse victims

candidates.summary: Russia’s Federal Security Service said it detained a Russian minor over an alleged threat to attack Moscow’s Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve after receiving information from the United States. The FSB said the minor had posted images from the reserve and videos showing tactical clothing and an object resembling an automatic weapon. The reserve, which had been evacuated and closed Saturday evening, reopened Sunday.
candidates.title: Russia detains minor after U.S. warning about Moscow park

candidates.summary: Seven OPEC+ countries—Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman—decided during a virtual meeting to maintain their September 2026 required production levels for December. The group said it would continue monthly reviews of market conditions and meet again on November 29.
candidates.title: OPEC+ countries maintain December oil-production targets

sources.name: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries

candidates.summary: Initial vote-count results indicated that acting President Iliana Yotova won Bulgaria’s presidential runoff against former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, who conceded defeat. The result remained subject to official confirmation; if confirmed, Yotova would become Bulgaria’s first woman elected president.
candidates.title: Initial results show Yotova winning Bulgarian presidential runoff

candidates.summary: Russian forces launched 433 drones at Ukraine from Saturday evening into Sunday, of which Ukraine’s air force said 371 were destroyed or suppressed. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes left hundreds of thousands of households without electricity. Ukrainian authorities also said a drone strike at a vocational-school site in Vinnytsia region killed three people, including a 13-year-old girl.
candidates.title: Russian drone barrage causes widespread Ukrainian power outages

candidates.summary: Iran’s Foreign Ministry designated Britain’s Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organizations and classified the Secret Intelligence Service, MI6, as a hostile group. The ministry said the measures took effect upon publication and were retaliation for British actions against Iran, including the United Kingdom’s treatment of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps under its State Threats Act.
candidates.title: Iran designates British naval and air forces as terrorist organizations

candidates.summary: The Paris prosecutor’s office opened an attempted-murder investigation after incendiary devices were thrown at a group of about 15 police officers and gendarmes during unrest following Saturday’s demonstrations. French authorities said more than 770 people were arrested nationwide after largely peaceful protests involving an estimated 320,000 participants ended in scattered violence.
candidates.title: France opens attempted-murder inquiry after attack on police

candidates.summary: Near-final Central Election Commission results, with 99.95% of polling-station protocols processed, showed acting President Iliana Iotova winning Bulgaria’s presidential runoff with about 57.6% of the vote against Andrey Gyurov’s 39.5%. Gyurov conceded, making Iotova set to become Bulgaria’s first woman elected president, subject to final certification.
candidates.title: Near-final count confirms Iotova’s Bulgarian presidential victory

candidates.summary: The United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara ceased operations after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate. The United Nations said November 1 marked the start of a liquidation period overseen by a smaller support team. The mission, established in 1991, had monitored the disputed territory and supported a ceasefire between Morocco and the Polisario Front.
candidates.title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years

candidates.summary: A Learjet 60 carrying nine people crashed at about 12:50 p.m. in Greenacres, Palm Beach County, killing everyone aboard. Authorities reported no immediate deaths or injuries on the ground. The jet had departed Austin, Texas, for the Bahamas, and its pilots reported icing and severe turbulence before the aircraft entered a steep dive. Federal investigators were sent to the site.
candidates.title: Nine killed in South Florida business-jet crash

candidates.summary: Israel’s Central Elections Committee chairman Noam Sohlberg said the October 27 parliamentary election was conducted properly and that even if suspicions of foreign interference were substantiated, they would not undermine the overall results. The statement, made alongside the attorney general and Shin Bet chief, followed unsupported claims by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party that Arab-led parties had stolen the election. The results still awaited formal certification.
candidates.title: Israeli election chief says vote results will stand

candidates.summary: Ukraine’s air force said the public Air Alert application was hacked late Sunday, briefly displaying false nuclear, chemical, radiation and street-fighting warnings in Kyiv and other regions, along with an erroneous warning about deployment of Russia’s Oreshnik missile. Officials said there was no radiation threat. The application was temporarily suspended while sirens and other public-warning systems continued operating.
candidates.title: Hack sends false emergency warnings through Ukraine air-alert app

candidates.summary: A six-day localized ceasefire around Russian-held Oleshky expired at midnight Moscow time after allowing deliveries and civilian evacuations. Ukraine’s human-rights ombudsman said both sides had upheld their obligations during the pause. Ukraine’s military separately said it evacuated 167 people, including 22 children, from threatened areas of the wider Kherson region. There was no immediate indication that fighting resumed when the truce expired.
candidates.title: Localized Oleshky ceasefire expires after evacuations

candidates.summary: Thousands of protesters led by opposition figure Rahul Gandhi marched in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a voter-list revision that removed more than 130 million names. Opposition parties alleged that the deletions disproportionately affected minorities and benefited the governing Bharatiya Janata Party. The Election Commission denied favoring any party and said eligible voters removed in error could re-enroll.
candidates.title: Thousands protest India’s voter-list revision

candidates.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians in two attacks in Gaza, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry. Medics reported three deaths in Gaza City, while the ministry said five police officers were killed in western Khan Younis. Israel’s military said it struck militants in Khan Younis but did not immediately comment on the Gaza City strike.
candidates.title: Israeli strikes kill at least eight people in Gaza
